neighbours.label: the connective between paired categories in social-science writing (formal and informal, intra- or inter-organizational)
fire: Power comes in several forms: formal and informal; legal authority or expertise.
Studies may look at either inter-group relations or outside networks.
Conformity has two sources: informational, and the wish to belong (normative pressure).
Status can be ascribed or achieved in most societies.
Groups can use both formal and informal rules of conduct.
Ties in a network are either strong or weak.
Leaders rely on task-oriented and relationship-oriented styles.
Norms may be explicit or implicit within an organization.
quiet: Dinner comes in several forms: hot and cold; rice or noodles.
Tours may go to either the old town or the outside markets.
The kitchen has two doors: front, and the one to the yard (back door).
Soup can be spicy or mild in most restaurants.
Kids can use both red and blue crayons at school.
Socks in a drawer are either clean or dirty.
Bakers rely on wheat flour and rye flour daily.
Shoes may be black or brown within a store.

notes: Card: ' and' x5, ' both' x3, ' of' x3, ',' x2, ' (', ';', ' either', ' provide'. Probes: 'formal and' 0.705, 'intra-organizational ties or' 0.552, ' (' before 'normative influence' 0.424; 'hot and cold' 0.009, 'Dogs mostly eat' 0.001. Near misses keep the sentence shape on everyday topics.
